/// A small task tracker.

use system.fs
use system.os
use system.collections.list

public class Task
    public var id int
    public var title String
    public var done bool

    public fn init(id int, title String)
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.done = false

fn find(tasks [Task], id int) Task?
    for task in tasks
        if task.id == id
            return Some(task)
    return None

fn read_commands(path String) [String]
    let fs = Fs()
    let contents = match fs.read_file(path)
        Result.Ok(text): text
        Result.Err(_error): ""
    return contents.trim_end().split("\n")

fn first_word(line String) String
    return line.split(" ").element_at(0)

fn rest_of(line String) String
    let head = first_word(line)
    if line.length() == head.length()
        return ""
    return line.substring(head.length() + 1, line.length())

fn main()
    let args = Args()
    var tasks = List<Task>()
    var next_id = 1

    for line in read_commands(args.element_at(0))
        if line == ""
            continue
        let command = first_word(line)
        let rest = rest_of(line)

        if command == "add"
            tasks.push(Task(next_id, rest))
            println(f"added {next_id}")
            next_id = next_id + 1
        else if command == "done"
            let id = rest.to_int() ?? 0
            match find(tasks, id)
                Some(found):
                    var task = found
                    task.done = true
                    println(f"done {id}")
                None: println(f"no such task {id}")
        else if command == "list"
            for task in tasks
                if not task.done
                    println(f"{task.id} {task.title}")

The stdlib has what I need: string `split`, `to_int`, `trim`, and list `length`/`push`. Before writing, here are the choices I'm making:

- **Priority buckets:** `list` loops priorities 0 to 9 and prints matching tasks. Tasks are stored in id order, so ties come out by id with no sort call.
- **Bad input:** `prio` checks the priority before looking up the id. Non-numeric or out-of-range `p` writes `bad priority <raw text>`.
- **Missing id:** it parses like `done` does, with `?? 0`.
- **Whitespace-only lines:** they are skipped, so they don't print `? `.

/// A small task tracker.

use system.fs
use system.os
use system.collections.list

public class Task
    public var id int
    public var title String
    public var done bool
    public var priority int

    public fn init(id int, title String)
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.done = false
        self.priority = 5

fn find(tasks [Task], id int) Task?
    for task in tasks
        if task.id == id
            return Some(task)
    return None

fn read_commands(path String) [String]
    let fs = Fs()
    let contents = match fs.read_file(path)
        Result.Ok(text): text
        Result.Err(_error): ""
    return contents.trim_end().split("\n")

fn first_word(line String) String
    return line.split(" ").element_at(0)

fn rest_of(line String) String
    let head = first_word(line)
    if line.length() == head.length()
        return ""
    return line.substring(head.length() + 1, line.length())

fn word_at(words [String], index int) String
    if index < words.length()
        return words.element_at(index)
    return ""

fn print_tasks(tasks [Task], include_done bool)
    var priority = 0
    while priority <= 9
        for task in tasks
            if task.priority == priority
                if include_done
                    if task.done
                        println(f"x {task.id} {task.title}")
                    else
                        println(f"- {task.id} {task.title}")
                else if not task.done
                    println(f"{task.id} {task.title}")
        priority = priority + 1

fn main()
    let args = Args()
    var tasks = List<Task>()
    var next_id = 1

    for line in read_commands(args.element_at(0))
        if line.trim() == ""
            continue
        let command = first_word(line)
        let rest = rest_of(line)

        if command == "add"
            tasks.push(Task(next_id, rest))
            println(f"added {next_id}")
            next_id = next_id + 1
        else if command == "done"
            let id = rest.to_int() ?? 0
            match find(tasks, id)
                Some(found):
                    var task = found
                    task.done = true
                    println(f"done {id}")
                None: println(f"no such task {id}")
        else if command == "prio"
            let words = rest.split(" ")
            let id = word_at(words, 0).to_int() ?? 0
            let priority = word_at(words, 1).to_int() ?? -1
            if priority < 0 or priority > 9
                println(f"bad priority {word_at(words, 1)}")
            else
                match find(tasks, id)
                    Some(found):
                        var task = found
                        task.priority = priority
                        println(f"prio {id} {priority}")
                    None: println(f"no such task {id}")
        else if command == "list"
            if rest == "all"
                print_tasks(tasks, true)
            else
                print_tasks(tasks, false)
        else
            println(f"? {command}")
